findings.reason: The 2026-09-20 AM scheduled run's `scripts/discover.py` sweep failed to query the arXiv API directly for both the 2026-09 and 2026-08 windows: export.arxiv.org returned HTTP 406 Not Acceptable to both requests (a different failure mode than the HTTP 429 rate-limiting seen on 2026-09-13). Crossref and OpenAlex succeeded for both windows (216+348 and 1462+1884 records respectively), so venue-published work for these months was still swept, but arXiv-native preprints not also indexed by Crossref/OpenAlex could have been missed. As a compensating spot-check, arxiv.org/list/cs.RO/2026-09 was fetched by hand via WebFetch (not itself blocked) and covered roughly the first ~130 listing entries (ids 2609.00001-2609.02134); the two humanoid-titled papers found there (2609.00677, 2609.02134) plus one more found in the same range (2609.01518) were already present in README.md from earlier runs, so this partial spot-check found no gap, but it does not cover the rest of September or any of August. A future run should re-sweep 2026-09 and 2026-08 through the arXiv API once the 406 clears, or extend the by-hand listing spot-check further into each month.

findings.reason: The 2026-09-20 AM scheduled run's `scripts/discover.py --refresh` pass (step 4, refreshing authors/abstracts on already-listed arXiv preprints and checking for venue promotions) failed outright: export.arxiv.org returned HTTP 406 Not Acceptable on its very first request, the same failure mode seen in this run's earlier discover.py sweep of the 2026-09/2026-08 windows (see the discovery-coverage-gap entry above), so this is one underlying block rather than two separate incidents. metadata-refresh.json was never produced, apply_promotions.py was not invoked, and no preprint-to-published promotions were checked or applied this run. A later run should retry step 4 once export.arxiv.org stops returning 406 to this environment.
